basics.name: Sreenath Krishnan Potty
basics.label: Electrical Engineer | Power Electronics Packaging | Reliability & Semiconductor Research
basics.summary: Electrical engineer with a master's degree from Virginia Tech and hands-on research experience in power electronics packaging, electrical insulation evaluation, partial discharge testing, and materials characterization. My work combines experimental testing, engineering analysis, and process development to support reliable electronic systems. My interests include semiconductor technologies, advanced manufacturing, and engineering project management.

education.institution: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, VA

education.thesis: Piezo-Tribo Nanogenerator (PTNG) for Powering Wearable Electronic Gadgets

work.company: Center for Power Electronics Systems (CPES), Virginia Tech
work.summary: Promoted from Laboratory Assistant while continuing hands-on research in power electronics packaging, dielectric insulation, and encapsulation; expanded responsibilities to student training and laboratory tours.
highlights: Continue partial discharge and dielectric insulation testing, materials processing, and experimental data analysis for power electronics packaging research.
Train incoming students in encapsulation workflows, including specimen preparation, vacuum degassing, curing, and electrical testing procedures.
Conduct laboratory tours, explaining research activities, equipment, and experimental workflows to visitors.

work.company: Center for Power Electronics Systems (CPES), Virginia Tech
work.summary: Conducted laboratory fabrication, insulation testing, and experimental analysis for power electronics packaging research.

projects.title: ONR — Evaluation of Insulation Degradation in 10 kV SiC Power Modules
highlights: Applied one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) design of experiments and statistical process analysis, including Shewhart methods and ANOVA, across more than 100 fabrication batches using MATLAB-based logging.
Developed and deployed an automated high-voltage testing workflow supporting over 3,000 tests and reducing testing cycle time by 46%.
Designed a laboratory test fixture that reduced fixture cost by 84%, and contributed to repeatable experimental procedures and process documentation.
Supported technical coordination and recurring progress reviews with a SiC device manufacturer.

projects.title: ARPA-E ULTRAFAST — E1 Arrester Press-Pack Module Assembly
highlights: Assembled press-pack SiC power-module subassemblies using documented manufacturing procedures and lot-level travelers, with 100% post-assembly qualification yield.
Evaluated package integrity through bond shear testing, thermal-interface-material profilometry, and electrical continuity checks.
Designed a 3D-printed thermal-interface-material cutting fixture to improve thickness consistency and reduce manual variability during assembly.

work.summary: Developed and evaluated system-monitoring software for a Smart Cluster Management Tool using Python and C in a UNIX/Linux environment.
highlights: Collaborated with hardware, software, and systems engineers to improve system monitoring accuracy by 30%.
Designed Python and C programs for real-time system performance monitoring and testing, contributing to a 10% reduction in system downtime.
Performed system-level testing and debugging, improving software stability by 15%.

volunteer.position: Volunteer — Bradley Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Virginia Tech
volunteer.summary: Volunteered with the Bradley Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Virginia Tech, supporting instructional resource development for electrical engineering coursework.
highlights: Developed MATLAB- and Python-based educational resources for ECE 3614 (Introduction to Communication Systems).

awards.title: KSCSTE Research Grant — Piezo-Tribo Nanogenerator
awards.awarder: Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment (KSCSTE)
awards.summary: Awarded a research grant by the Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment (KSCSTE) in support of undergraduate research on a flexible piezoelectric–triboelectric nanogenerator for wearable electronics.

projects.title: Project Lead, Programmer - Rental Forecasting Tool
projects.organization: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
projects.summary: Developed a forecasting tool using Python and statistical methods to predict rental demand, increasing decision-making accuracy by 20%. Led a multidisciplinary team, ensuring project delivery on time and 17% under budget. Generated an ROI of 2,126%, delivering $217,212 in value from an investment of $9,760. Integrated data analysis and visualization techniques using Python and Google Colab, providing real-time insights on rental trends.

projects.title: MEMS Engineer - MEMS Fabricated Continuous Sweat Glucose Monitor
projects.organization: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
projects.summary: Engineered a MEMS-fabricated, glucose sweat sensor, improving lifespan by 700% over commercial models. Simulated sensor behavior using COMSOL Multiphysics. Experimented with techniques like photolithography, Physical Vapor Deposition(PVD), Atomic Layer Deposition(ALD), Chemical Vapor Deposition(CVD), and reactive ion etching to fabricate the sensors.

projects.title: Packaging Engineer - Embedded Package Design of a 100V GaN HEMT Device for EV Applications
projects.organization: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
projects.summary: Designed a GaN HEMT packaging solution that optimized thermal management by 25%, improving electrical performance under high-stress conditions. Conducted electrical and thermal simulations using LTSpice and Ansys Q3D to troubleshoot design flaws and reduce parasitic inductance by 10%. Led the failure analysis testing and validation of the packaging design, including wire bond pull tests, reducing failure rates by 20%.

projects.title: Electrical Engineer - Two-Stage Differential Amplifier
projects.organization: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
projects.summary: Designed and simulated a two-stage differential amplifier using TSMC 180nm PDK, reducing power consumption by 12%. Optimized transistor sizing to meet stringent specifications, improving overall circuit efficiency by 10%. Conducted post-layout simulations in Cadence Virtuoso, ensuring compliance with industry standards. Analyzed extracted simulations, identifying key areas for optimization, enhancing performance.

projects.title: Project - Piezo-Tribo Nanogenerator (PTNG) for Powering Wearable Gadgets
projects.summary: Developed an energy-harvesting nanogenerator, optimizing material configuration to improve energy conversion efficiency by 30%. Simulated the nanogenerator model using COMSOL Multiphysics, troubleshooting issues and ensuring compliance with design specifications. Presented findings at ICMSMT 2021, demonstrating innovation in renewable energy and showcasing strong documentation, presentation, and communication skills.
